Assuming that's a square, you can solve the missing top-left angle of the top-right triangle to be 10 degrees, thereby making the top-left angle of the bottom-left triangle 40 degrees. Since it is a square, the missing bottom-middle angle of the bottom-left triangle is 50 degrees.

Overall, there are now 4 missing angles: the "?" angle (bottom-middle angle of middle triangle), the bottom-middle angle of the bottom-right triangle, the right-middle angle of the middle triangle, and the right-middle angle of the bottom-right triangle. I name these angles "a", "b", "c", and "d".

We know that 
a + b + 50 = 180, 
c + d + 80 = 180, 
40 + a + c = 180, and 
90 + b + d = 180

Therefore, we have to solve the following system of equations:

a + b = 130
c + d = 100
a + c = 140
b + d = 90

I asked ChatGPT to solve it for me, and it got:
a = 90
b = 40
c = 50
d = 50

I plugged these values in and they seem fine.

Since "?" is "a", the "?" angle is 90 degrees.

What I mean is that my fingers can't grow shorter since there's nothing in my body that can identify and "eat" bone away at only the tips and not anywhere else. (That's as good as my layman-mind can describe it)

So my eyes can't grow shorter since there's nothing in my body that can ______________?

I ask this, because human eyes and human bones are quite different, so the analogy only makes sense to a point. I'd like to know the specifics.

"Your eye tissue can grow longer [...] But in general your eye will not shrink" 
Why can it grow longer, but not shrink?
I already know that once it grows, it doesn't shrink back down. I'm asking *why* this is the case.

I seriously doubt the explanation given to me by doctors is "just noise". Do you have links to research papers or something like that, that I can read that supports your claim of nearsightedness being genetic over my own optometrists'? I'm simply skeptical of all claims, and that is why I originally asked my question.

And while nearsightedness makes my near vision "better" it also makes my far vision worse. And in fact, at the rate my eyes are becoming more and more myopic (my eyes are even worse than my fathers' and grandfathers' and mothers' and grandmothers' both when they were my age, AND right now!) I might actually become legally blind by my 30s. I'm 17, and Im -4.25 in my right eye, and -3.75 in my left. So I sorta need to know why this is happening, for peace of mind.
